scenarios.description: Nominal healthy baseline with standard sensor noise (0 mV bias, 0 mOhm)
scenarios.explanation: All diagnostic residuals (voltage slope: 0.60 mOhm, rest offset: -11.94 mV, thermal excess: -2.34 deg C) are well within healthy calibration bounds.

scenarios.description: Increased internal resistance (+22 mOhm contact/electrolyte degradation)
scenarios.severity_estimate: +22.3 mOhm internal resistance increase (+80.1% vs baseline)
scenarios.explanation: Voltage sag is strongly coupled to load current (slope dV/dI = -22.32 mOhm), while zero-current resting residual is negligible (-11.88 mV). This matches an Ohmic / contact degradation mechanism without sensor bias.

scenarios.description: Abnormal thermal rise (80% cooling loss + 2.0W micro-short heat flux)
scenarios.severity_estimate: +12.1 deg C average thermal excess above convective equilibrium (peak +29.4 deg C)
scenarios.explanation: Cell temperature exceeded expected thermal equilibrium by an average of +12.06 deg C (peak rise rate: 2.99 deg C/min). This indicates a thermal management failure (e.g. cooling loss or unexpected heat generation).

scenarios.description: Capacity fade (22% active lithium loss, retention = 0.78)
scenarios.severity_estimate: 22.7 % usable capacity loss relative to baseline
scenarios.explanation: The cell delivered 22.7% less Ah throughput before voltage cutoff than the baseline reference model expected, while internal resistance remained near baseline. This points to active lithium inventory loss (capacity fade).

scenarios.description: Positive voltage sensor bias (+45 mV ADC calibration offset)
scenarios.severity_estimate: +33.2 mV constant voltage sensor calibration offset
scenarios.explanation: A persistent static voltage residual of +33.25 mV is observed even at zero current (rest), and is relatively independent of load current fluctuations (r=+0.194). This distinguishes an ADC / analog front-end calibration bias from physical electrochemical aging.

scenarios.description: Negative voltage sensor bias (-35 mV ADC reference drop)
scenarios.severity_estimate: -46.5 mV constant voltage sensor calibration offset
scenarios.explanation: A persistent static voltage residual of -46.50 mV is observed even at zero current (rest), and is relatively independent of load current fluctuations (r=+0.178). This distinguishes an ADC / analog front-end calibration bias from physical electrochemical aging.
